html:
CRYPTO NEWS — August 24, 2026

Bitcoin and Ethereum are grinding higher in selective strength, with BTC holding $77K and ETH crushing it at $2,455. The 7-day rally is real—BTC +21.60%, ETH +28.90%, SOL +24.10%—but total market cap dropped 1.22% in 24h, meaning capital is concentrating in the big names while alts languish. Fear & Greed jumped to 73 overnight, funding is flat at 0.0100% across the board, and stablecoin reserves sit solid at $256.6B. This is a controlled move higher, not a blow-off. Traders are cautious despite the greedy sentiment reading.

TODAY'S HIGHLIGHTS

Bitcoin posts largest weekly dollar gain in history as momentum holds above $77K
BTC logged its best week in dollar terms since records began, riding 21.60% gains and staying pinned between $76,464–$78,013 with tight 24h action. This kind of weekly move typically attracts new money but also triggers profit-taking; the fact that funding stayed flat suggests leverage wasn't driving the rally. The setup: If BTC breaks and closes above $77,500 next 24h, momentum likely extends to $78K resistance. If it dips below $76,464, watch for a flush to shake out weak longs—that's your signal funding may flip negative.

Ethereum outpaces Bitcoin with 28.90% weekly gain; golden cross narrative resurfaces
ETH's 1.82% daily gain beat BTC's 0.78%, and the weekly 28.90% outrun shows alts are playing catch-up after a dormant summer. The "golden cross" technical setup (50-day above 200-day MA) is classic bull-flag material, but it's also a contrarian signal that smart money has already positioned. ETH dominance sitting at 11.3% means there's room for rotations if sentiment stays greedy. Trade it: Expect ETH to either consolidate around $2,450–$2,482 or gap higher on any positive macro news (Jackson Hole this week). A break below $2,406 overnight flips the bias bearish fast.

Ray Dalio and institutional voices call for Bitcoin allocation as U.S. debt risks mount
The recurring macro narrative—rising Treasury debt, Fed policy uncertainty, geopolitical friction—keeps pushing institutional players toward BTC as a hedge. Dalio's "own a bit of Bitcoin" comment is establishment permission slip language; when billionaires talk inflation hedges on Sunday shows, retail hears "free money." This matters for your trade because it sustains bid under dips. Watch Jackson Hole (this week) for any Fed signals that would either confirm the macro thesis (bullish for BTC) or pivot to rate-cut delay (potential short-term pullback before the bigger move).

MORPHO jumps 16.9% to $2.76 on protocol momentum; isolated strength amid broader consolidation
While BTC and ETH grind higher, MORPHO's sharp 24h move suggests sector-specific catalysts (lending, governance, or accumulation) independent of the macro tape. This is a reminder that individual tokens can spike hard in low-volume conditions, especially when Fear & Greed is high and traders are fishing for 2-5x plays. Takeaway: Don't chase isolated pumps without checking daily volume and resistance levels. MORPHO's gain is noise relative to the $2.60T market, but it flags that money is rotating—some is leaving established pairs for yield or governance plays.

WATCH LIST

Monitor BTC resistance at $77,500–$78,013 over the next 24h. A clean break and daily close above $77,500 extends the weekly rally and could trigger stop-loss buys up to $79K. Conversely, any dip below $76,464 in the next 6 hours will test trader conviction; funding stays neutral but Greed at 73 is a yellow flag for pullback risk. ETH must hold $2,450; failure there invites a retest of $2,406 support. Jackson Hole economic symposium drops this week—watch Fed speakers for any hawkish surprises that would short-circuit the rally. Stablecoins remain ample ($256.6B), so if sentiment flips, there's ammo for a flush. SOL holding near $94 suggests it's being used as a rotation play rather than leading; if it breaks $92.96, expect broader alt weakness.

See you tomorrow — stay sharp and don't marry the momentum.
